proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8082 pānīya documents pāni/pāṇi “water”; its addendum explicitly includes Western Pahari “water, rain”. Where a survey uses the same local form for water and rain, that recorded polysemy supports the rain response’s link to the water family. Same language, locality tags and normalized form are recorded for water: f_wyfc77jojeego. The exact regional route may include borrowing between Indo-Aryan languages; the supported family is linked under the user’s preference.

Survey y/j forms and proximal plurals are paradigm continuations with analogical remodeling; no direct mechanical derivation of each inflected form from nominative eṣa is asserted.
